item.title: Chamath says open AI models are "commoditize your complement." Agree?
item.excerpt: Chamath's argument (https://research.socialcapital.com/p/open-vs-closed): companies give away the thing they dont sell for free, so the thing they do sell is worth more. Meta makes money though ads, Google and Microsoft from cloud. The losers are companies whose business is selling access to closed models. But still companies are paying more and mroe for closed models anyway! Does this theory hold up?

item.title: Rpi – a Rust rewrite of the Pi agent, 10× faster startup
item.excerpt: I've been learning about the Pi agent and decided to rewrite it in Rust. Now that I've finished a lot of the work, I'd like to show how much faster Rust (rpi) is than TypeScript (Pi). Here are the results: | Metric | rpi (Rust) | Pi (TypeScript) | Difference | |:---|:---|:---|:---| | `--version` | 17.5 ms | 169.5 ms | 9.7× faster | | Cold start | 17.7 ms | 189.5 ms | 10.7× faster | | RSS when ready | 12.0 MiB | 91.5 MiB | 7.6× smaller | | Install size | 21.8 MiB | ~385 MiB | ~18× smaller | Rust is really cool!

item.title: How we closed 1,500 GitHub issues in one month
item.excerpt: Millions of developers use Next.js, and the issue tracker is one of the main ways we learn where they run into problems. It receives an average of 36 new reports each week. […] The backlog peaked at 3,109 open reports in January 2025. […] By August 10, 2026, it still had 2,244. […] Fixed bugs, duplicates, and reports about unsupported versions were burying current regressions. […] Roughly three weeks later, we'd closed 1,462 issues across the repository and brought the backlog below 1,000, even as 218 new reports arrived. […] Here's the history since 2017: To work through that many issues, we built an agent to research the backlog. […] In January 2025, with the backlog at its peak of 3,109 issues, we added a workflow that marked an issue stale after two years without activity (later 18 months) and closed it after a grace period. […] By August 10, 2026, it had helped bring the backlog down to 2,244. […] An old issue might be fixed, a duplicate, expected behavior, or about something we no longer support. item.title: OpenClaw 2026.10.1 fixes duplicate Telegram deliveries
item.excerpt: OpenClaw 2026.10.1 fixes a bug where messages queued before a gateway restart could be delivered twice to Telegram chats. The issue affects macOS installations managed by launchd that restart the gateway while deliveries are pending. Upgrade to 2026.10.1; no configuration change is required.

item.title: Telegram bot tokens abused through misconfigured webhooks
item.excerpt: Attackers are actively abusing Telegram bot tokens leaked through misconfigured public webhook endpoints. Bots that use long polling instead of webhooks are not exposed by this issue. Operators of affected bots should rotate their tokens and restrict webhook endpoints.
